{{Current events|year=2021|month=02|day=8|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces resume an [[Ma'rib Campaign|offensive]] against [[Maʼrib]], the last stronghold of the internationally-recognized [[Government of Yemen|Yemeni government]] in northern Yemen. A government source says that 20 pro-government fighters have been killed and 28 others have been injured repelling five attacks in the past 24 hours. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/yemen-houthis-offensive-marib-stronghold (''Middle East Eye'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty-four workers die in a [[flood|flooded]] illegally-run [[textile]] workshop in a private house in [[Tangier]], [[Morocco]], which occurred as a result of intense rains that hit the region. Ten others were rescued and hospitalized. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/8/more-than-20-dead-in-morocco-underground-factory-flood (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
******[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that [[restaurant]]s can bring back their indoor dining from February 12, three days ahead of originally schedule on [[Valentine's Day]] Sunday. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/new-york-city-indoor-dining-to-resume-friday-11612821741 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****The [[Houston Methodist Hospital]] reports [[Texas]]' first case of the 501.V2 variant in a man from [[Fort Bend County, Texas|Fort Bend County]] who recovered several weeks ago. This makes it the fourth state known to have this variant. [https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/houston/article/The-South-African-variant-of-COVID-19-has-arrived-15934362.php (''The Houston Chronicle'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[United States|U.S.]] [[United States Secretary of Transportation|Transportation Secretary]] [[Pete Buttigieg]] quarantines for 14 days after a member of his security detail tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/02/08/pete-buttigieg-quarantine-member-security-team-tests-positive/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] resumes morning news conferences two weeks after testing positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://apnews.com/article/medication-mexico-health-coronavirus-pandemic-mexico-city-ea6d77a115ef49c197d88f4421e9c6e3 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 13,038 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 963,028. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5366073/rekor-13038-sembuh-kasus-aktif-covid-19-ri-ada-171288-per-8-februari (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] receives 300,000 doses of [[China]]'s [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2064675/laos-receives-300-000-vaccine-doses-from-china (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 24 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 896. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/02/08/malaysia-records-highest-daily-death-at-24-with-3100-new-covid-19-cases-in/1948046 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[Seoul]] metropolitan government launches [[COVID-19]] test for pet cats and dogs, which comes after [[South Korea]] reported its first case of COVID-19 infection in an animal ([[kitten]]) on January 24. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-seoul-launches-tests-for-pets-14138894 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****[[France]] introduces new measures to ban homemade masks in [[education in France|educational]] institutions, requiring school children over the age of six to only wear category 1 masks in schools. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20210208-ban-on-homemade-fabric-masks-comes-into-effect-in-french-schools-covid-19 (RFI)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****The [[Netherlands]] extends its nationwide curfew until March 3 in order to prevent the spread of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://apnews.com/article/world-news-netherlands-coronavirus-pandemic-dc8e693f15d80c9ab7cf5a1acb58b7ed (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Cyprus]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Northern Cyprus]] reports its first case of B.1.1.7 variant in 16 samples that contracted [[SARS-CoV-2]] variant first detected in the United Kingdom. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/covid-19-variant-found-in-northern-cyprus/2138177 (Anadolu Agency)]
***The [[European Commission]] finalizes a deal to secure 300 million additional doses of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-vaccine-eu-orders-300-million-more-pfizer-shots/a-56502706 (DW)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[Lineage P.1]]
***[[Argentina]] reports its first cases of two different [[Brazil]]ian [[variants of SARS-CoV-2|SARS-CoV-2 variants]] in two people infected with the P.1 variant and two others infected with the P.2 variant. [https://www.semana.com/coronavirus/articulo/argentina-detecta-una-nueva-variante-del-coronavirus/202101/ (Semana)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
***[[Rwanda]] eases its [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in the capital [[Kigali]] and allows businesses to resume operations with up to 30% of essential staff. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/rwanda-eases-covid-19-lockdown-in-capital/2137274# (Anadolu Agency)]
*The [[Government of Vietnam|government]] of [[Vietnam]] reports that it has culled more than 100,000 [[poultry]] in 14 [[provinces of Vietnam|provinces]] so far this year in a bid to contain the spread of highly pathogenic [[H5N1]] and [[H5N6]] bird flu strains. [https://www.reuters.com/article/vietnam-birdflu/vietnam-culls-100000-poultry-as-bird-flu-outbreaks-spread-idUSL4N2KE1GZ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Greece–Israel relations]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
**[[Prime Minister of Greece|Greek Prime Minister]] [[Kyriakos Mitsotakis]] and [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] sign an accord that would allow vaccinated travellers to visit freely between the two countries without any restrictions in order to revive their battered tourism sector. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/262149/article/ekathimerini/news/greece-israel-sign-agreement-on-tourism-during-pms-visit (Ekathimerini)]
*[[Russia–European Union relations]], [[2021 Russian protests]]
**The governments of [[Cabinet of Germany|Germany]], [[Politics of Poland|Poland]], and [[Government of Sweden|Sweden]] each [[Persona non grata|expel]] a Russian diplomat to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]]'s expulsion of three [[European Union]] diplomats on February 6. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/02/08/germany-poland-sweden-to-expel-russian-diplomats-in-tit-for-tat-move-a72868 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Trial of Benjamin Netanyahu]], [[corruption in Israel]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] pleads not guilty to [[criminal charge|charges]] of [[bribery]], breach of trust and [[fraud]] at the Jerusalem District Court. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-netanyahu-trial/netanyahu-pleads-not-guilty-to-corruption-as-trial-resumes-idUSKBN2A80JP?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Venezuelan refugee crisis]]
**The [[Government of Colombia|government]] of [[Colombia]] announces the legalization of undocumented [[Venezuela]]n migrants currently in the country, making them eligible to receive 10-year residency permits. [https://apnews.com/article/access-to-health-care-health-statutes-colombia-venezuela-7767509edf281a6e0b394d4b0b187eca (AP)]
*[[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election]], [[Trump–Raffensperger phone call]]
**[[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] officials launch a investigation into former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] for several phone calls made urging officials such as [[Georgia Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Brad Raffensperger]] to overturn [[Joe Biden]]'s win in the state. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/08/us/politics/trump-georgia-election-investigation.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]], aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**A nationwide [[general strike]] takes place in [[Myanmar]] in response to the military coup with thousands marching in the capital [[Naypyidaw]], where they clashed with [[riot police]]. Several injuries have been reported. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-55975746 (BBC)]
**The [[State Administrative Council|military junta]] declares [[martial law]] in the country's second largest city [[Mandalay]] amid protests against the coup. Public gatherings of more than five people are banned, and a [[curfew]] from 8 pm until 4 am has been imposed. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/martial-law-parts-myanmar-protests-military-coup-mandalay-14140170 (Channel News Asia)]
*[[2021 Somali presidential election]]
**An alliance of opposition parties ceases recognising [[Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed]] as the [[President of Somalia]], and propose the creation of a "national council of lawmakers, opposition leaders and civil society" to govern the country as the President's term expires with no clear plan for succession. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-election/somalias-opposition-cease-recognising-president-as-election-row-escalates-idUSKBN2A80OD?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2018–2021 Haitian protests]]
**Haitian opposition names judge [[Joseph Mécène Jean-Louis]] from the [[Supreme Court of Haiti|Supreme Court]] the new interim [[President of Haiti]] to lead a "transitional government" after arguing that incumbent [[Jovenel Moïse]]'s term has expired and calling on him to step down. The [[Organization of American States]] considers that Moïse's five-year term ends in 2022 as he took office in 2017. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/08/americas/haiti-opposition-president-term-protests-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Palau National Congress]] passes a joint resolution supporting the decision made by [[President of Palau|President]] [[Surangel Whipps Jr.]] to leave the [[Pacific Islands Forum]]. The National Congress says that the "gentleman's agreement was not honored". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/435992/palau-congress-backs-withdrawal-from-pacific-forum (RNZ)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Australian Open]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**The [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] of the [[Australian Open]] begins in [[Melbourne Park]], three weeks later than originally scheduled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]], with daily attendance capped at 30,000 people per day. [https://7news.com.au/sport/tennis/australian-open-serves-up-quiet-day-one-c-2120076 (7 News)]
